title: Data Profiling, Quality Gates & Query Folding
summary: Leverage column quality histograms, whitespace/error traps, and Query Folding best practices across large database refreshes.
learningObjectives: Diagnose hidden null/whitespace mismatches in merge joins using Power Query profiling
Order M transformations (`Filter` before `Transform`) cleanly to keep SQL Query Folding active

sections.heading: 1. Column Profiling & Order-Sensitive Folding
sections.content:
Silent join mismatches often come from invisible trailing spaces (`'Sales '` vs `'Sales'`) or mixed case (`'usa'` vs `'USA'`), turning `100%` expected matches into silent orphans. Trimming, cleaning control characters, and standardizing case BEFORE merging prevents data gaps.

Just as critical for SQL/Warehouse connections: **Transformation Ordering** dictates whether Query Folding survives! Placing foldable SQL steps (`SelectColumns`, `Filter`, `Group`, `Sort`) FIRST before non-foldable local M steps (`Index` or custom regex) lets the remote database discard 99% of unnecessary historical data cleanly over the wire.

codeExamples.code:
[SQL Server Source (100M rows)]
   |--(Foldable: Filter Year >= 2025 + Select 4 cols)--> Pulls ONLY 2M clean rows!
   |--(Non-Foldable first! e.g. Custom Index before Filter)--> Pulls 100M rows -> Timeout Crash!
codeExamples.explanation: Keep database-pushdown foldable predicates at the very top of Applied Steps so source engines prune irrelevant history cleanly.

keyPoints: Audit column distribution and quality indicators (>1,000 rows view in Power Query bottom status bar!)—don't profile strictly on top 1,000 rows!
Trim and normalize casing cleanly prior to Distinct / Merge steps.
commonMistakes: Adding an Index Column at step 2 before filtering years at step 5—silently disabling Query Folding over 50M rows!

sections.heading: 2. Defensive Merge Keys & Null Coalescing
sections.content: See cleanly how ordering trims and filtering prior to adding derived keys preserves fast remote query folding.

codeExamples.code:
let
  Source = Sql.Database("warehouse.corp.local", "AnalyticsDB"),
  RawOrders = Source{[Schema="dbo", Item="Orders"]}[Data],
  // 1. Prune rows and columns FIRST (maintains 100% Native SQL Query Folding!)
  RecentOrders = Table.SelectRows(RawOrders, each [OrderDate] >= #date(2025, 1, 1)),
  SelectedCols = Table.SelectColumns(RecentOrders, {"OrderId", "RegionCode", "OrderDate", "Amount"}),
  // 2. Normalize join keys cleanly
  CleanRegion = Table.TransformColumns(SelectedCols, {{"RegionCode", each Text.Upper(Text.Trim(_)), type text}})
in
  CleanRegion
codeExamples.explanation: Selecting needed columns and date bounds immediately yields a lightweight native SQL `SELECT ... WHERE` upstream.
codeExamples.expectedOutput: Fast remote SQL filtered extraction with normalized RegionCode keys

keyPoints: Click 'Column profiling based on entire data set' inside Power Query before shipping schemas to avoid missing late-file edge nulls.
commonMistakes: Leaving auto-generated `'Changed Type'` steps injecting dozens of hardcoded columns that crash if upstream tables rename minor unused fields.

exercises.title: Rescue Broken Query Folding in a 50M-Row Refresh
exercises.objective: Reorder Applied Steps to restore Native SQL Query Folding.
exercises.description: A nightly refresh pulling from Azure SQL fails with memory timeout after 90 minutes. Applied Steps shows: `1. Source -> 2. Add Custom Index -> 3. Filter Country = 'IN' -> 4. Remove 25 unused columns`.
instructions: Identify the step destroying SQL Query Folding.
Rewrite the exact step sequence allowing SQL Server to execute column pruning and filtering before local operations run.
hints: Remove unused columns and filter Country FIRST before adding local Index columns.
exercises.submissionRequirements: Complete all checklist items, test assumptions, and document verification rationale.
evaluationCriteria: Addresses the root architectural/technical challenge accurately
Follows defensive industry standards and edge-case validation
exercises.solutionExplanation: Filtering `Country = 'IN'` and pruning 25 columns upfront drops transferred rows cleanly, enabling the optional Index to run rapidly strictly on surviving records.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why did placing `'Add Index Column'` before `'Filter Date >= 2026'` cause a 50M-row SQL import to time out?

options.text: Row index numbering breaks Query Folding, forcing Power Query to fetch all 50M rows over the network before filtering locally
Dates cannot appear after integer columns in VertiPaq
SQL Server bans filtering integer indexes

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Apply row/column pruning first while Query Folding stays active.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: By default, Power Query's visual column quality preview profiles how many rows unless explicitly switched?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: Errors or rare nulls appearing past row 1,000 stay hidden unless full-dataset profiling is enabled.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Why apply `Text.Trim()` and uniform casing to text category keys before performing merges/relationships?

options.text: Eliminates silent trailing spaces and casing discrepancies that break joins cleanly
Removes the need for a Date dimension

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Whitespace mismatch creates silent orphan rows and duplicate legend entries in visuals.

recap: You guarded joins against whitespace/casing drift and structured fast foldable ETL pipelines.
